item.title: BREACH, One Week Later: Twelve Seasons, Your Own Home, and Forty-Six Real Incidents
item.description: What changed in BREACH in a week. The campaign now ends on the defender’s side, eleven new seasons go well beyond AI, season 10 leaves companies for a family home with a “to do at home” card in every debrief, season 12 audits a vibe-coded app, and the community store holds forty-six case files inspired by real incidents. Plus a call for the first mission written by someone other than me.

item.title: One Year Later: I Asked a Stronger Model to Review My Vibe-Coded App
item.description: I built Cyber Code Academy in December 2025 with Cursor and Copilot, and had the AI of the time check its security. One year later, a single prompt to Claude Opus 5.5 found 50 problems, two of them critical. Anyone could delete the challenges, and any learner could fake their own test results. The bugs, the fixes, the redesign, and a second prompt that showed the exercises were unfair too.
